newsitem.title: FINLAND: Sampo sees rise in 1996 premium income.
newsitem.headline: Sampo sees rise in 1996 premium income.

text.p: Finnish insurer Vakuutusosakeyhtio Sampo said on Wednesday it expected premium income to rise by over three percent this year against 1995.

"Positive news of increasing durable goods consumption and the pick-up in investments mean that full-year premium income is expected to rise over three percent," Sampo said in its January-June interim report.
In the first half, Sampo's domestic direct insurance premium income increased slightly more than three percent to 2.84 billion markka.
In 1995, total group premiums written, including reinsurance, were 4.22 billion markka.
Direct insurance premium income was expected to increase at the pace of the market's growth. As a result, Sampo expected to retain its 35 percent market share, it said.
"The group's steady result development, excellent solvency, and the improved liquidity of the shares are likely to reflect positively on the second half of the year, too," Sampo said.
